extracted.intended_audience: federal executive-branch agencies and agency officials (agency heads, OMB/OIRA); also regulated parties
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for creating, publishing, reviewing, rescinding, and using agency guidance documents and for transparency/fairness in civil administrative enforcement and adjudication. Applies to executive-branch agencies' processes, OMB/OIRA oversight, and public notice/comment obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance documents treated as non-binding
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must treat guidance documents as non-binding both in law and in practice, except as authorized by law or as incorporated into a contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy statement: guidance documents may clarify obligations but should not impose legally binding requirements; agencies should state that guidance lacks the force and effect of law (also required explicitly by Sec.4(a)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public input and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should take public input into account when appropriate in formulating guidance documents and make guidance documents readily available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: public notice and availability helps ensure fair regulatory process and adequate notice of obligations; avoid issuing guidance without adequate distribution or posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding requirements only through regulations or adjudications
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may impose legally binding requirements on the public only through regulations (proper notice-and-comment rulemaking) or on parties case-by-case through adjudications, and only after appropriate process, except as authorized by law or incorporated into a contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: using guidance documents to regulate without following APA rulemaking procedures; guidance should not carry implicit threats of enforcement to coerce compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'guidance document' and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'guidance document' means an agency statement of general applicability intended to have future effect on regulated parties that sets forth policy or interpretations, but excludes: rules promulgated under section 553, rules exempt under 553(a), rules of agency organization/procedure/practice, decisions of agency adjudications, internal guidance not intended to have substantial future effect on regulated parties, and internal executive-branch legal advice/opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to determine whether an instrument is a guidance document subject to these procedures; several common agency materials are explicitly excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant guidance document tests
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'significant guidance document' is one that may reasonably be anticipated to: (i) have an annual economic effect of $100 million or more or materially affect economy, sectors, productivity, competition, jobs, environment, public health/safety, or state/local/tribal governments/communities; (ii) create a serious inconsistency or interfere with another agency's action; (iii) materially alter budgetary impact of entitlement/grant/user-fee/loan programs or rights/obligations of recipients; or (iv) raise novel legal or policy issues arising from legal mandates, the President's priorities, or EO 12866 principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance determination triggers heightened procedures (see Sec.4(a)(iii)). Agencies should evaluate guidance against all four subtests when deciding whether it is 'significant.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and treatment of pre-enforcement rulings
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'pre-enforcement ruling' is a formal written communication in response to an inquiry about compliance that interprets or applies law to a specific set of facts (includes informal guidance under SBREFA section 213, letter rulings, advisory opinions, no-action letters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-enforcement rulings are explicitly defined and are treated differently in some respects (Sec.4(a)(iii) and Sec.5 do not apply to pre-enforcement rulings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single searchable indexed guidance database
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 120 days of OMB's implementing memorandum, each agency or component must establish or maintain on its website a single, searchable, indexed database that contains or links to all guidance documents in effect for that agency or component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The website must note that guidance documents lack the force and effect of law except as authorized by law or incorporated into a contract. All existing and future guidance must be included in this database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and rescission of existing guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 120 days of OMB's implementing memorandum, each agency must review its guidance documents and, consistent with law, rescind those it determines should no longer be in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No agency may retain guidance in effect without including it in the database; agencies may not cite or rely on rescinded guidance except to establish historical facts. An agency may reinstate a rescinded guidance within 240 days under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Director waiver and reporting authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The OMB Director (or designee) may waive compliance with database/review requirements or extend deadlines for particular guidance documents or categories, and may request reports from agency heads explaining reasons for maintaining guidance in effect (to be provided to the President).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should expect OMB oversight and possible directed reporting regarding retained guidance; compliance deadlines are subject to OMB discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to promulgate internal procedures/regulations for issuing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 300 days of OMB's implementing memorandum, each agency shall, consistent with law, finalize or amend regulations to set forth processes and procedures for issuing guidance documents that are consistent with this order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must codify processes for issuing guidance, including explicit items required in the regulation (see subsections (i)-(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear statement of non-binding effect on each guidance document
rubrics_metrics.description: Each guidance document must clearly state that it does not bind the public, except as authorized by law or as incorporated into a contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required element of agency procedures and of each guidance document (Sec.4(a)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public petition process for withdrawal or modification
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures must include procedures for the public to petition for withdrawal or modification of a particular guidance document, including designation of the officials to which petitions should be directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must identify responsible officials and a transparent process for petitions challenging guidance documents (Sec.4(a)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice-and-comment and agency response for significant guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: For significant guidance documents, unless exigency/safety/health/compelling cause warrants exemption, agencies must provide at least 30 days public notice and comment before issuing a final guidance document and must publicly respond to major concerns raised in comments (unless agency makes a 'good cause' finding and incorporates that finding and brief reasons into the guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This imposes an APA-like notice-and-comment process for significant guidance, with a minimum 30-day comment period and required public responses to major issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-delegable approval for significant guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant guidance documents must be approved on a non-delegable basis by the agency head or by an agency component head appointed by the President before issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior-level sign-off is required for significant guidance to ensure accountability (Sec.4(a)(iii)(B)).

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA review prior to issuance of significant guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant guidance documents must be reviewed by the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA) under Executive Order 12866 before issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIRA review is required unless agency and Administrator agree exigency/safety/health/compelling cause warrants exemption. OIRA also may issue memoranda establishing categorical exceptions and presumptions of significance (Sec.4(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with executive-order regulatory review requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant guidance must comply with the applicable requirements for regulations or rules (including significant regulatory actions) set forth in Executive Orders 12866, 13563, 13609, 13771, and 13777.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat significant guidance consistently with executive-order standards for regulatory review, cost-accounting, international regulatory cooperation, regulatory cost control, and regulatory reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA authority to define exceptions and significance presumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator shall issue memoranda establishing exceptions from this order for categories of guidance documents and categorical presumptions regarding whether guidance documents are significant, and may require submission of significant guidance documents to OIRA for review before agency regulations are finalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIRA has authority to create broad or categorical rules (and exceptions) about which guidance is subject to heightened procedures; agencies should follow OIRA memoranda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of EOs 12866, 13563, and 13609 to guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements and procedures of Executive Orders 12866, 13563, and 13609 shall apply to guidance documents, consistent with Section 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must harmonize guidance-document procedures with those Executive Orders, subject to specified exceptions and OIRA determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation by OMB Director via memoranda and regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OMB Director shall issue memoranda and, as appropriate, regulations pursuant to statutory authority to provide guidance regarding or implement this order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should expect further implementing instructions and possible regulatory requirements from OMB to operationalize the Executive Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: General limitations, implementation constraints, and non-enforceability
rubrics_metrics.description: The order must be implemented consistent with applicable law and appropriations, does not impair authority granted by law to agencies or the Director's functions, and is not intended to create any right or benefit enforceable in law or equity against the United States or its agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to interpret the order: it cannot override statutory authority and does not itself create private rights of action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated exceptions where the order does not apply
rubrics_metrics.description: The order does not apply to actions pertaining to foreign or military affairs or national/homeland security functions (except certain procurement/import/export guidance), to criminal investigations or prosecutions (including undercover operations), to civil enforcement or related DOJ investigations, to investigations of employee misconduct or employment actions, to documents/information exempt from FOIA disclosure (5 U.S.C. 552(b)), or to other circumstances where agency head determines application would undermine national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should identify and document when a guidance document or action falls within an exception; these exceptions limit the scope of procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and fairness in civil administrative enforcement and adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall act transparently and fairly with respect to all affected parties in civil administrative enforcement or adjudication; regulated parties must know in advance the rules by which the Government will judge their actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchored in APA and FOIA principles: ensure prior public notice of jurisdiction, publish substantive rules/statements of general policy/interpretations in the Federal Register when required, and avoid adverse effects from unpublished rules unless person had actual and timely notice (5 U.S.C. 552(a)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements under FOIA and APA
rubrics_metrics.description: The Freedom of Information Act generally requires agencies to publish substantive rules of general applicability, statements of general policy, and interpretations of law in the Federal Register; FOIA also generally prohibits agencies from adversely affecting a person with an unpublished rule or policy except if the person has actual and timely notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For enforcement and adjudication, agencies must be mindful of FOIA/APA publication and notice obligations to uphold fairness and prevent ad hoc unpublished determinations (Morton v. Ruiz cited).
